findings.title: SSD Advisory - Samsung MagicINFO Unauthenticated RCE
findings.summary_md: An independent researcher working with SSD Secure Disclosure published an unauthenticated arbitrary file upload in Samsung MagicINFO 9 Server 21.1050.0 via the /MagicInfo/servlet/SWUpdateFileUploader endpoint, where a path-traversable fileName parameter allowed a JSP web shell and remote code execution under Apache Tomcat. SSD notified Samsung on 12 January 2025, received a duplicate notice, and released the advisory with a working curl proof of concept against port 7002 after its 90-day window and grace period expired. This is the original researcher disclosure in the chain that Samsung later assigned SVE-2025-50001 / CVE-2025-4632.

findings.title: Rapid Response: Samsung MagicINFO 9 Server Flaw
findings.summary_md: Huntress independently verified that the then-latest MagicINFO 9 Server versions 21.1050.0 and 21.1040.2 were still exploitable with the public SSD Disclosure proof of concept, concluding the August 2024 patch for the earlier CVE-2024-7399 was incomplete or covered a separate flaw. The post reported exploitation already occurring in the wild, cited Arctic Wolf's observation of exploitation, and noted a Mirai botnet variant exploiting the flaw tracked by the SANS ISC. Huntress advised keeping MagicINFO 9 Server off the internet until a proper fix shipped.

findings.title: Post-Exploitation Activities Observed from the Samsung MagicINFO 9 Server Flaw
findings.summary_md: Days after the proof of concept went public, Huntress documented three exploitation incidents beginning 2025-05-04 among more than 75 customer machines with MagicINFO installed. Attackers downloaded php_cli.exe and srvany.exe from 185.225.226[.]53 and registered a LocalSystem service named PHP5.3.8 under C:\MagicInfo Premium\tomcat\bin for persistence. The post points to System event log Event IDs 7045 and 7000 as detection anchors and lists SHA256 hashes for the dropped binaries.

findings.title: CVE-2025-4632 Detail
findings.summary_md: NVD published CVE-2025-4632, a CWE-22 path traversal in Samsung MagicINFO 9 Server before 21.1052 that lets attackers write arbitrary files with system authority, scored 9.8 CRITICAL by both NVD and CNA Samsung. The record references Samsung's SVP-MAY-2025 security update (SVE-2025-50001) as the vendor advisory and fix. The page also flags the CVE as present in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

findings.title: Samsung MagicINFO 9 Server Path Traversal Vulnerability (CISA KEV)
findings.summary_md: CISA added CVE-2025-4632 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 22 May 2025 under the entry name Samsung MagicINFO 9 Server Path Traversal Vulnerability, with a required-action due date of 12 June 2025 for federal civilian agencies under BOD 22-01. KEV listing confirms the vulnerability was known to be exploited in the wild at the time of addition.
